original_manifest.provenance: None. Run 36844232498's 'Record release manifest' step failed before writing manifest.json (python3: Argument list too long, exit code 126), so no release-manifest-0.1.0-beta.12 artifact exists for this version.

release_evidence.reason: Release run 36844232498 published every artifact, passed registry-install verification on all eight Node targets and Chromium, and created annotated tag v0.1.0-beta.12, but its Record release manifest job failed: 'Build and record the manifest' died with 'python3: Argument list too long' (exit code 126) because release.yml passes the merged artifact digests to scripts/release-manifest.py as a single command-line argument that exceeded the Linux per-argument limit, the same defect as beta.8 (#799); the follow-on upload step then found no manifest.json. Issue #1115 tracks it. There is therefore no original manifest to preserve. This record rebuilds it with the repository's own scripts/release-manifest.py from the inputs the run did preserve: the registry-state and artifact-digest values printed in the failed job's log for the npm core, wasm, crates and PyPI publishers, the registry-state-native-* and artifact-digest-native-* artifacts, and the support-matrix-drift artifact, all from run 36844232498. It adds the release_evidence this repository's manifest job does not itself populate (tag, per-registry checksums, workflow run references, clean-install verification), assembled from the run's own jobs plus registries independently checked live on 2026-10-01. No registry_state value is corrected: every entry is the run's own recorded value.

empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: AI21 states no prefix, length or alphabet, and its SDK does no validation. The 32-alphanumeric shape rests on one peer rule (Vulnetix vnx-sec-315) and two independent implementations (keychecker, LLM-Runner-Router) that accept exactly [A-Za-z0-9]{32}, plus a ten-sample maintainer observation (#784). AI21 staff committed six key literals to public example code (2023-2025), each 32 mixed alphanumerics and none a UUID; their validity is unknown, and whether a provider-committed literal counts as a provider example is maintainer ruling Q-AI (redact-secret#1013), pending, so they are not counted. The value has no marker of its own, so it is claimed only beside a same-line AI21 name, host or SDK constructor. No pinned scanner has an AI21 rule, and no provider-issued key has been measured.

supportedContexts: .env / shell export / CI or compose environment assignment (GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_PAT, RENOVATE_TOKEN)
Authorization: Bearer header and an octokit debug log 'token ' header value
JSON (composer auth.json) and Terraform provider token string
bare github_pat_ value anywhere on a line (the prefix is the marker)
gh auth login --with-token stdin
git remote URL userinfo and git credential fill output
values with and without a leading '11' in segment 1 (neither is asserted)
empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: GitHub documents only the github_pat_ prefix (docs 'GitHub's token formats'); no GitHub page states the 22 + '_' + 59 body. The grammar is corroborated by three GitHub-owned redaction and DLP rules (which redact, never generate or validate), one full-length value in GitHub's own REST 'Revoke a list of credentials' example, two pinned peer rules (osv-scalibr, trivy) and four independent validators. A GitHub product manager endorsed the exact regex in community discussion 36441 (2022-10-24); whether that staff reply (R3) or the GitHub-owned code (R1/R9) is a T1 grammar statement is maintainer ruling Q-GH (redact-secret#1013), pending, so the family stays T2. No checksum, fixed '11' lead or GHES parity is claimed, and peer rules that admit other widths (trufflehog 36-255, CredSweeper 80-255, \w{82}) are recorded as supersets. No provider-issued token has been measured.

supportedContexts: same-line mailchimp keyword assignment (e.g. MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=<value>), bare, double-quoted, or after a CRLF comment line
suffix -us + one or two digits (no other data-center literal is claimed)
empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: Mailchimp states the shape only by examples: its fundamentals page shows a 31-hex-character body with -us6, and its own WordPress plugin shows 32 hex with -us19, matching every tool and 111 of 115 public-code candidates (redact-secret#699); the contract follows the 32-byte example. The fundamentals page says the data center is always appended as key-dc. Hex case and the data-center alphabet (only us<N> is ever shown) are not stated by the provider. The only staff statement (2009) advises against regex validation because keys may change. Non-us data-center literals and g-z body letters are outside the claim since 2026-09-24 (docs/decisions/2026-09-24-stop-asserting-provider-undecided-format-properties.md): no scored fixture asserts them either way, so the product's handling of them is unmeasured.

supportedContexts: Authorization: Bearer on a line naming the Mistral API host
same line as the word mistral, e.g. MISTRAL_API_KEY=, api.mistral.ai, Mistral(api_key=...)
empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: Mistral states no prefix, length or alphabet in prose and its SDK does no validation. Its own Admin API OpenAPI schema (APIKeyExtendedOUT, synced to the docs 2026-07-24) shows one full-length example key: 32 alphanumeric characters, no prefix. Three tool rules (osv-scalibr, betterleaks, pleno-dlp) read as one assertion of 32 alphanumerics beside a Mistral name, and three independent client validators (GitLens, GPTPortal, NeuroLink) accept exactly ^[A-Za-z0-9]{32}$. The value has no marker of its own, so it is claimed only beside a same-line Mistral name, host or constructor. GitGuardian lists a second, prefixed 'Mistral AI API Key v2' with an undisclosed prefix that no Mistral source mentions. No pinned scanner has a Mistral rule. No provider-issued key has been captured through #205 intake.

The 58 + T3BlbkFJ + 58 width (133 characters) rests on four peer owners: trufflehog 3.97.4's dedicated openaiadmin detector, gitleaks 8.30.1 (whose three admin vectors are 58/58), nuclei-templates and poltergeist. empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: Okta states no length or alphabet in prose. It shows the token as an elided SSWS example beginning 00, and three dated, distinct full-length examples in its own repositories (developer docs guide, management OpenAPI spec 2025-2026, an API-security book page 2019), all 00 + 40 alphanumeric. A 2019 devforum answer ('always 42 characters', regex 00 + 40 [a-zA-Z0-9-_]) comes from an account whose staff status is not confirmed on the forum. Both 2023 items in this record come from one devforum thread (2023-09-21): an Okta team reply saying not to assume a set structure (and that there are no plans to change it) and a customer's alphabet reading. gitleaks' '=' comes from its generic AlphaNumericExtended helper, not from Okta evidence, and GitGuardian does not treat 00 as a prefix. The four open contradictions below carry the dispositions redact-secret#1013 proposes, pending maintainer ruling Q-OK; until ruled they stay unresolved. No issued token has been measured.

empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: No Together page, staff statement or SDK code states the tgp_v1_ prefix, a length or an alphabet. The shape rests on one scanner rule (betterleaks; Kingfisher aliases it, so it is one lineage, not two) and a four-sample maintainer observation (#783). No pinned scanner (trufflehog 3.97.4, gitleaks 8.30.1) has a Together rule. No provider-issued key has been captured through #205 intake. A 2026-09-27 re-check of the broad-discovery sources for #783 (Reddit, Stack Overflow, GitHub code and issue search, Hacker News, and the scanner repos trufflehog main, gitleaks master, GitGuardian ggshield, osv-scalibr, secretlint, pleno-dlp and two general leak-scanner projects) found no new source for the tgp_v1_ shape itself; betterleaks/Kingfisher and #783 remain the only two owners. It did find that pleno-dlp (github.com/plenoai/pleno-dlp, tag v0.66.4, commit b3cd17fa41953a98aaafaa61aa8ab3e05882bf66) ships a Together detector for a different, sibling shape (a bare 64-character lowercase-hex string, keyword-gated on 'together'), which the corroboration decision's own rule ('a rule for a sibling shape does not count') excludes from this family's corroboration count; it is recorded below as evidence toward the open legacy-key contradiction instead.
